chunks: From him, from Yusuf ibn Aqil, from Muhammad ibn Qays, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said:
The Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) said: 'Do not eat the slaughtered meat of the Arab Christians, for they are not People of the Book.'

key_terms.ذَبِيحَةَ: slaughtered meat (specifically that which is slaughtered)

ai.seo_question: Why are Arab Christians not considered People of the Book for the purpose of eating their slaughtered meat in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* highlights a specific juristic distinction where Arab Christians are excluded from the general permissibility of *Kitabiyah* meat, likely due to their distinct tribal and religious identity separate from the broader 'People of the Book' category. It reflects the Shia scholarly view that 'Ahl al-Kitab' refers specifically to Jews and Christians who maintain their scriptural lineage, whereas certain Arab groups may not qualify under strict definitions. This ruling underscores the importance of contextualizing religious identity in dietary laws within Islamic jurisprudence.
